fieldValues.title: Every release can open every repository that exists
fieldValues.decision_question: When the stored form of SRS data changes (a new dataModelRevision), in what order may its parts land, so that no release leaves existing repositories unreadable?
fieldValues.context: A stored-form change is already ruled to be a migration (srs rfc-decision-628cf6c4, 'A rename is a migration': a deterministic migration plus a generation stamp). What was never ruled is when the migration ships relative to the code that reads the new form. The srs CLAUDE.md revision-bump choreography assumes 'the binary loads old AND new revisions', but as a convention, not a decision. The gap stopped srs-rust#1417 (RFC-052, revision 10): its plan split the loader from the migration, and by RFC-052 [R7] the loader alone would refuse every existing repository. The builder escalated it as bbb03bff, a question about that one issue. The owner asked (session 2026-10-22) that decisions be framed as the lasting practice rather than the task, so this decision states the practice and bbb03bff is answered by it.
fieldValues.friction: A binary that reads only the new form makes every existing repository unreadable until the migration follows; holding the release instead blocks every unrelated fix behind it.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: Do nothing: each revision bump re-argues its PR shape, and a split like #1417's first plan can make master unreleasable. A temporary dual-read loader in each revision: smaller PRs, but interim code to carry and remove every time. Merge the loader and hold the release until the migration lands: master stops being releasable for everything else in between.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Support for a new data-model revision lands in the same change as the migration that brings older corpora to it, so master is always releasable and no release refuses data it cannot also migrate. A change that only prepares for a revision may land ahead of it, provided it alters no behaviour. This refines srs rfc-decision-628cf6c4 (a stored-form change is a migration). It applies to RFC-052 (srs-rust#1417), RFC-051 (srs-rust#1414) and every later revision.
fieldValues.rationale: Repositories are held by many tools and people at once; a release that cannot open them breaks all of them at the same moment. The revision-8 change (srs-rust#1144) already landed this way, and the release corpus gate (migration pending on a refused corpus) presumes it.
fieldValues.revisit_when: When a revision's migration cannot be written in the same change as its reader (for example, it needs data only a later tool can supply).
fieldValues.next_steps: Set aside bbb03bff as answered by this decision. srs-rust#1417 lands as a behaviour-neutral prep PR, then revision 10 with its migration in one PR. Cite this decision in srs CLAUDE.md's revision-bump choreography.
